rationale: C10 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both letters concern the Administration's foreign-economic legislative program and argue that a major trade measure should not be considered hurriedly late in the current session, but should receive full committee hearings and early consideration the following year. They also share the same legislative audience—the House Ways and Means Committee—and a parallel progression from stressing the program's importance, to explaining why immediate consideration is unwise, to endorsing prompt action next year. C14 has a similar timing rationale but lacks the child's specific committee-and-hearings machinery. C20 is substantively connected to the proposed trade organization but does not share the child's legislative scheduling structure as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I share your view that it would be ill-advised to launch consideration of H.R. 5550 in your Committee when so little time remains in this session. A matter of this vital importance should have thorough hearings, discussion and debate.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Accomplishing enactment of the heart of the program...would, I believe, best be served by careful and deliberate action taken on the basis of extensive and unhurried hearings.
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same concrete rationale: an important foreign-trade measure should not be rushed and requires extensive committee hearings.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I am pleased indeed to have your assurance that H.R. 5550 will be among the very first measures to be considered by your Committee next year.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It is my hope and expectation that the Committee on Ways and Means...will initiate consideration...so that full and adequate hearings may be completed between now and the convening of the Congress next January. Under this procedure the prospect for consideration by the Congress early next year is excellent.
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts C10's scheduling machinery involving Ways and Means, hearings, and priority consideration early the next year.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Committee on Ways and Means has borne a heavy burden of difficult and constructive legislation in this session of Congress. Much of that constructive effort has been concerned with legislation implementing various parts of the Administration's program in the field of foreign economic policy.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: In addition to initiating hearings on the vital subject of extension and amendment of the Trade Agreements Extension Act, there is much else that should be accomplished in this session of the Congress to carry into effect the recommendations of my Message of March thirtieth.
shared_material.explanation: Both situate the requested trade action within the larger Administration foreign-economic legislative program and the committee's existing workload.
